messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: P1 - Third-party auth provider degradation (Auth0). High error rate on token introspect and token verification calls causing user login failures and admin console access issues. Root TS: 1718704321
Maya Chen: I'm oncall, looking. Saw the spike in token_verification.error and 401s in auth-proxy metrics. Confirming impact on login flows.
Liam O'Connor: Booting into auth-proxy logs and tracing. Can you paste a representative error?
Maya Chen: tail from auth-proxy logs:
```
auth-proxy | 2026-02-19T18:12:02Z ERROR token_introspect failed status=502 upstream_url=https://acme-tenant.auth0.com/introspect message="upstream 502"
```
Nora Patel: Auth0 status page shows an incident: https://status.auth0.com/incident/abcd — they reported service degradation in their token introspect endpoint. No ETA on full recovery.
Maya Chen: Initial plan: (1) Increase session TTL to reduce introspect frequency, (2) enable JWKS caching to avoid remote calls when possible, (3) enable emergency local-admin console accounts so engineers/customers can access admin UI. Applying step 1 now.
Sam Rodriguez: How do we enable emergency local-admin accounts quickly for prod?
Maya Chen: Run these commands: `redwood-admin feature-flag set allow_local_console true --env prod` then create a user: `redwood-admin user create --email oncall+admin@redwood.ai --role admin --password "<secure-password>"` — rotate creds after incident.
Jess (SRE): I'm preparing a hotfix to use cached JWKS for signature validation and fall back to cached introspect results for a short window. Pushing to canary (auth-verifier-canary).
Maya Chen: Support/CS: prepare customer comms. Post a short message on status.redwood.ai once we have mitigation in place.
SupportBot: Suggested status page blurb: "We're experiencing login disruptions caused by our external auth provider. We've applied mitigations to restore access for most users and are monitoring. Affected customers will be notified individually if impacted."
Liam O'Connor: Canary patch looks promising — token verification error rate dropped from ~70% to ~12% in canary pods.
Maya Chen: Rolling patch to 30% then full if stable. Also applying a rate limiter on introspect calls in auth-proxy to avoid cascading upstream failures: `--introspect-rps=10`.
Nora Patel: Auth0 support case opened: Case ID 54233. They requested tenant logs and examples of failing requests. Sending logs now.
Maya Chen: Uploaded relevant logs to secured gist (redacted): https://gist.github.com/redacted. Notifying Auth0 support and engineering contact.
Sam Rodriguez: Customer impact summary so far: ~1.2k sign-in failures in 30m window; 23 enterprise customers reported console access issues (notably AcmeCorp, SlateApp). CSMs notified to do outreach for affected customers.
Jess (SRE): Added temporary JWKS caching with TTL 10m and local introspect cache for 60s to reduce dependency pressure. Monitoring metrics.
IncidentBot: Please annotate milestones: mitigation_start, canary_success, full_rollout, auth0_recovery.
Liam O'Connor: Milestones: mitigation_start=06:20 UTC (JWKS caching canary), canary_success=06:40 UTC (errors down to 12%), full_rollout=07:12 UTC (errors <5%), auth0_reported_recovery=07:30 UTC (Auth0 status updated to partial recovery).
Maya Chen: Handoff note: I'll hand over to Liam at 06:30 UTC once the first mitigation is confirmed. Leaving monitoring and customer comms to oncall.
Liam O'Connor: Taking over at 06:30 UTC. Current state: mitigations up, canary healthy, rolling out to all verifier pods. Continuing to monitor token error rate and backend latency.
Nora Patel: Runbook consideration: add a fast path for top-tier customers — create service account tokens or temporary local accounts for admin access if external SSO fails. Support to coordinate identity docs with CSM.
Maya Chen: Agreed. Support: prepare template for invite-only bypass and record which customers accepted bypass.
SupportBot: Updating incident timeline and customer list in the incident doc.
Jess (SRE): Created incident postmortem doc stub: /incidents/auth-provider-2026-02-19.md (will include timeline, impact, mitigations, action items).
Liam O'Connor: Auth0 confirms they rolled a fix for a routing misconfiguration that caused their introspect endpoints to return 502s. They marked the incident resolved on their side at 07:28 UTC. We continued to monitor for 2 hours to ensure stability.
Maya Chen: Postmortem action items: 1) Implement always-on JWKS caching with monitored TTL and automatic refresh jitter, 2) Build robust local introspect fallback (cached results + allow short-lived local tokens), 3) Add external auth-provider SLO alerting (rate and error thresholds), 4) Quarterly tabletop for third-party dependency outages.
Jess (SRE): Adding those to tasks and assigning owners in the postmortem doc.
Liam O'Connor: Final check: no signs of credential leakage, no anomalous token exchange patterns. Recommend security review only if new evidence emerges.
Maya Chen: Closing operational thread — will move final write-up to /postmortems and ping mailing list. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
